title: Synthesis and Tribological Characteristics of High-Performance Self-Lubricating CoCrFeNiMo<sub>x</sub>-Ni/MoS<sub>2</sub>-Ag-Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Composites.

recollection.starting_material: Powders of the CoCrFeNiMo_x high-entropy alloy together with Ni-coated MoS2, elemental Ag powder and Cr2O3 particles
recollection.intervention: Mechanical alloying/blending followed by vacuum hot-pressing or spark-plasma sintering to form a bulk self-lubricating composite
recollection.structure: A dense CoCrFeNiMo_x solid-solution matrix containing uniformly dispersed Ni/MoS2 lamellae, discrete soft Ag inclusions and fine hard Cr2O3 particles
recollection.mechanism: During sliding the Ag and MoS2 migrate to the contact surface forming a low-shear transfer film while the hard Cr2O3 and solid-solution strengthening from Mo maintain hardness; the combined action lowers friction and wear
recollection.results: Typical reported numbers (guess): room-temperature friction coefficient 0.10–0.15 (≤0.2 up to 600 °C) and wear rate ≈1–3 × 10⁻⁶ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹, with composite hardness around 450–500 HV and compressive strength above 1.3 GPa, outperforming the Mo-free CoCrFeNi matrix whose friction is ≈0.5 and wear an order of magnitude higher

score.note: The recollection identifies powder blending and SPS as the fabrication route but misses that the central intervention was varying Mo content among x = 0.2, 0.5, and 1. Its structure description is largely a generic constituent dispersion and omits Mo-induced lattice distortion, the Mo-rich σ phase, boundary-localized additives, and high-temperature glaze formation. The Ag/MoS2 low-shear film and Mo strengthening mechanisms are substantially correct, though the σ-phase contribution and oxide/silver-molybdate tribofilms are omitted. Most numerical claims are unsupported or wrong: the minimum friction was 0.23 at 800 °C, wear was much higher at 400 °C, hardness reached 546 HV, and the reported yield strengths were about 443–502 MPa rather than compressive strength above 1.3 GPa.
